title: Indicators: Nature's Colour Code
summary: Litmus, turmeric, china rose, red cabbage, phenolphthalein and methyl orange: how indicators work and how to choose one.

ib.note: Good MYP Criterion B/C task: making a natural indicator

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 2: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic and Neutral (litmus, turmeric, china rose)
Ch 2: Acids, Bases and Salts (phenolphthalein, methyl orange, olfactory indicators)

objectives: I can describe the colour changes of natural and synthetic indicators in acids and bases.
I can explain why some indicators (like turmeric) can only detect bases.
I can choose a suitable indicator for a task and justify my choice.
I can plan how to make and test a natural indicator.
misconceptions: One indicator can always tell acid, base and neutral apart.
Turmeric turning red means an acid is present.
Indicators change the substance they are added to.
